Generate a Daily Ukraine–Russia War Analyst Brief for today's date.

This report is for analysts supporting the Department of War / OUSW Comptroller Program/Budget office. Write it as a 10-minute read, analyst-grade, executive-quality product.

RESEARCH WINDOW: Last 24-48 hours only. Use background only when needed to explain a current development.

REQUIRED REPORT STRUCTURE:

PART I — SENIOR LEADER SNAPSHOT
---

Provide 3-5 bullets: What changed in the last 24-48 hours? What matters most? What may affect U.S. funding, defense articles, stockpiles, or readiness? Any Ukraine-Russia / Operation Epic Fury overlap?
Each bullet: Source name | Direct link | Confidence: High/Medium/Low/Cannot confirm

5-7 bullets tagged: [Funding] [Appropriations] [Execution] [PDA] [USAI] [Defense Articles] [Stockpiles] [Replenishment] [Congressional RFI] [Readiness] [Epic Fury / Iran Linkage]
Each: What happened | Why it matters | Likely congressional question

5 watch items: Indicator to watch | Why it matters | Budget/defense article/congressional implication | Link

## MOST LIKELY CONGRESSIONAL RFI QUESTIONS TODAY
5-10 questions likely to be asked based on today's reporting.

Each: Topic tag | One-sentence summary | Why it matters | Source | Link | Confidence

Frontline changes, Russian offensives, Ukrainian counteroffensives, missile attacks, drone attacks, air defense, cyber, Black Sea, Crimea, casualty reporting (only if credible).

## 3. DEFENSE ARTICLES, WEAPONS, STOCKPILES, AND MUNITIONS
A. U.S.-Provided Defense Articles — Patriot, NASAMS, HIMARS, GMLRS, ATACMS, Javelins, Stingers, 155mm, 105mm, Bradleys, Abrams, Strykers, MRAPs, air defense radars, counter-UAS, drones, EW, F-16 support, spare parts
B. Allied/Partner Defense Articles — NATO, UK, Germany, France, Poland, Baltic states, Nordic, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea
C. Stockpile and Readiness Issues — depletion, shortages, replenishment delays, multi-theater demand competition
D. Analysis for each: What article? Transfer/requested/depleted/delayed/replenished/produced? Impact on battlefield? Impact on U.S. readiness? Congressional interest? Appropriations implication?

## 6. OPERATION EPIC FURY / IRAN AND UKRAINE-RUSSIA WAR LINKAGE
A. Weapons and stockpile competition — Patriot/THAAD/SM/NASAMS interceptors, counter-drone, PGMs, ISR
B. Drone/missile warfare linkage — Iranian drones in Ukraine, Shahed-type systems, ballistic threats
C. Russia-Iran relationship — weapons cooperation, diplomatic support, tech transfers, sanctions evasion
D. Energy and economic effects — oil prices, LNG, Hormuz, Black Sea, European energy security
E. Strategic bandwidth and force allocation — CENTCOM vs EUCOM, congressional appetite, allied burden sharing
If no credible connection confirmed, state: "I cannot confirm a direct linkage between Operation Epic Fury and the Ukraine-Russia War in today's reporting."

## 12. SOURCE LOG
Table: # | Source | Title | Date Published | Link | Topic | Confidence | Notes
EVERY source must have a direct working web link. No source without a link. Label paywalled, official source, analysis, or claimed (for Russian/Ukrainian official claims).

## 13. CONFIDENCE MATRIX
Table: Claim/Topic | Confidence | Reason
Definitions — High: official source or multiple credible sources. Medium: credible single source, not independently confirmed. Low: single-source, unclear, disputed. Cannot confirm: insufficient reliable sourcing.

---
SOURCE RULES:
- Every claim must have a source with a working web link.
- Do not state something as fact if it cannot be confirmed.
- Clearly label: Confirmed | Likely | Claimed but unverified | Disputed | Cannot confirm
- Prioritize: U.S. Government releases > ISW > CSIS/RAND/RUSI/Atlantic Council > Reuters/AP/BBC/FT/WSJ/NYT/WaPo > DefenseNews/Breaking Defense/USNI > Kyiv Independent/Ukrinform
- Label Russian MoD and Ukrainian MoD claims as claims, not confirmed facts.
- No political commentary. No speculation without evidence. No sensational language.
